Maya / Aditya — I pulled the account timeline and exported the usage. Summary: EdgeBeam has requested three separate trial top-ups over the past 90 days — 2026-09-02 (25k approved), 2026-10-11 (50k approved), and yesterday's email (requested 200k). Usage patterns show bursts from two primary IP blocks and several new sign-ins from similar email aliases. See attached trial_history_report.pdf and audit_log_export.csv.

My read: borderline for manual escalation. They have real engagement (calls, demo) but the cadence of repeat top-ups is higher than our standard pilot profile. Ben — can you run a quick abuse/fraud signal check? If we see account linkage or scripted token consumption we should deny a large top-up.

-Neha
Senior AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: trial_history_report.pdf, audit_log_export.csv
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T08:55:00Z
Subject: RE: Request for additional trial credits — fraud signals

Team — ran the signals overnight. Key findings:
- Account tie-ins: two sign-ins share device fingerprints with an older flagged account from 2026-06 that had abnormal top-up patterns.
- Payment/contact: billing contact is a free corporate alias; no billing verification on file.
- Consumption signature: sustained, high-throughput token consumption consistent with automated benchmarking (steady ~3k tokens/min over 14-minute windows).

I also pulled the MAU exception request Alice attached in the portal (mau_signed_exception.pdf). The request looks legitimate in form, but the behavioral telemetry is concerning. Recommendation: do NOT approve the 200k top-up. Offer a guarded extension: 25k for focused validation under monitored conditions + require Ops to run tests from a single whitelisted IP / timebox of 48 hours. If they pass, escalate for a larger approved grant after KYC.

-Ben Carter
Fraud & Abuse Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: mau_signed_exception.pdf
From: maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request for additional trial credits — decision and next steps

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick responses and for sending over the MAU exception. We want to support your evaluation but also protect the program from potential scripted abuse. Here's what we can do immediately:

1) We will issue a monitored 25k token extension scoped to a single IP range and a 48-hour window. Redwood will collect telemetry and flag any automated consumption patterns.
2) If the run is purely exploratory and remains within the expected cadence, we can consider a further 150k grant but only after a short KYC call (confirming team members, billing contact, intended workload) and a passing telemetry check.
3) Please have your Ops team reply to this thread with the single IP range and preferred 48-hour window by EOD tomorrow.

If you cannot comply with the whitelisting / KYC steps we will have to deny the larger top-up.

Regards,
